text:
Maya: quick design question — for SDK surface: should we unify streaming + paginated polling into one API, or split them? thinking about retries, resume semantics, and language ergonomics.

Sam: split. Streaming = push/subscribe style with short-lived connection and cancel token. Polling = discrete page calls with explicit resume cursors. different failure modes.

Liam: +1 on split. Polling needs deterministic idempotency and windowed retries (so servers can GC cursors). Streaming should expose heartbeats and reconnection hooks, not automatic page replays.

Anna: practical concern: a lot of users want an "auto-retry" iterator for pagination in Python/TS/Go. can we provide a safe default that won't accidentally replay user-visible state (e.g., payments or side-effects)?

Maya: exactly. proposal: paging endpoints return opaque cursor + "cursor_ttl" (seconds). SDK page iterator will retry transient network errors within the cursor_ttl using idempotency token. After ttl expires, iterator surfaces a special error and stops. Streaming connections do reconnect but only resume if server indicates "stream-resumable" with stable offset.

Sam: sounds reasonable. minor: use idempotency token + last-seen-offset in each request for poll retry. token protects against server-side double-apply; offset ensures you don't re-fetch/skip.

Liam: sketch python surface (pseudo):
```python
# polling / paginated
for page in client.list_items_streaming_aware(query):
    for item in page.items:
        handle(item)

# streaming (server streaming websocket/sse)
async for event in client.stream_items(channel):
    process(event)
```
Note: list_items_streaming_aware returns a normal iterator that will automatically backoff/retry inside cursor_ttl, but raises CursorExpiredError when ttl passes.
```

Anna: TS/Go shapes should mirror that ergonomics but with explicit cancellation:
```ts
// TS: async iterator for pages
for await (const page of client.listItems({q})) {
  page.items.forEach(x => ...)
}

// streaming
const stream = client.streamItems({channel});
stream.on('data', ...);
stream.on('end', ...);
```
```go
// Go: channel-based streaming vs paged client
ch := client.StreamItems(ctx, opts)
for ev := range ch { ... }

it := client.ListItems(ctx, opts)
for it.Next() { item := it.Item(); ... }
```

Maya: important policy points we need in docs and SDK:
- default: automatic retries for idempotent read-only paginated endpoints within cursor_ttl only.
- if endpoint is not purely read-only, require user to opt-in to automatic replay via explicit parameter.
- SDKs must expose hooks so callers can observe each retry attempt (metrics/tracing).
- server must return opaque cursor and cursor_ttl; TTL <= 5m by default.

Sam: how do we surface partial page commits? i.e., user processes items and crashes mid-page — on retry they may re-process first N items. Should we try at-least-once or exactly-once?

Liam: pragmatic: default at-least-once with idempotency guidance in docs. Provide helper helper that can checkpoint by last-processed-item-id and pass that as a resume-anchor to the next request. That helper can be a mixin in SDKs.

Anna: agree. add a small helper in SDK: `cursor = client.checkpoint(cursor, last_processed_id)` that returns a new cursor safe to replay from after crash.

infra-bot: deploy plan note — server will need a new field `cursor_ttl` and a `resumable` flag on streaming endpoints. rollout: server can start returning fields backward-compatible; SDKs should treat missing fields as non-resumable.

Maya: decision summary for RFC follow-up:
- split streaming vs pagination APIs on SDK surface.
- pagination: opaque cursor + cursor_ttl. SDK auto-retries within ttl using idempotency tokens; expose CursorExpiredError when ttl elapsed.
- streaming: reconnect logic only if server marks `resumable`; otherwise surface disconnect. Provide reconnect backoff hooks.
- provide language helpers for checkpointing to reduce duplicate processing.
- document opt-in for automatic replay on non-read endpoints.

Sam: small implementation note: for JS/TS, make the paging iterator be an async generator so it's natural for `for await` and easy to attach tracing.

Liam: for Go, keep the iterator methods explicit `Next()/Item()/Err()` shape so we can avoid hidden goroutine reconnection complexity. explicit is better there.

Anna: I'll draft SDK changes and a short compatibility guide. will include sample errors (CursorExpiredError, StreamNotResumableError) and recommended server defaults.

Maya: perfect. @Anna please ping when you have the sketch — I'll add it to the RFC follow-up doc and tag eng-runtime to update server bits. :+1:
